A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniMedVL and retain identifiable methods, experiments and appendix material. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete documents, including revised tables and image-based analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original UniMedVL benchmark results, curriculum ablations, reconstruction experiments and expert evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds external generation evaluation, segmentation comparisons, fine-tuning results, a blinded realism study and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The curriculum, dual encoders, CAG/DCOT and frozen VAE remain. However, Section 3.3 replaces the description of MoT experts with cross-attention by specialized FFNs with shared self-attention. The loss also loses its explicit weighting coefficient, although both appendices retain CE:MSE weights of 0.25:1.0. The PDFs do not establish whether these differences reflect implementation changes or revised descriptions.

E1.justification: V3 adds an external generation scenario using datasets described as excluded from training, plus quantitative segmentation evaluation on KiTS, QaTa, BUSI, CVC, Glas, ISIC, Kvasir and REFUGE. The expert audit also drops microscopy from its modality coverage. The renamed training corpus and retained five VQA benchmarks do not themselves constitute new coverage.

E2.justification: The main VQA comparison adds MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B/32B, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4 and Gemini-2.5-Flash. V3 also evaluates four modality-specialized generators, SAM3 and Medical SAM3, and a fine-tuned FLUX VAE comparator. The MIMIC-CXR comparison substantially changes membership, removing proprietary/general understanding models while adding Hulu-Med, QoQ-Med and additional unified models.

E3.justification: New protocols include VQA fine-tuning under two scoring conventions, Dice-based segmentation evaluation, a blinded 100-image study with two experts, and controlled efficiency measurements. Report generation removes RadCliQ−1 and adds several BLEU, METEOR and ROUGE metrics. Retained interleaved-task tables redefine the dagger as a fine-tuning variant despite unchanged scores; this is a reported setting change, not evidence of rerunning those experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct VAE fine-tuning diagnostics, small-lesion reconstruction checks, external-distribution evaluation, protocol comparisons, efficiency analysis and extensive generation/editing/understanding failure analysis. These substantially broaden the questions examined. Conversely, most entries in Tables 8–11 redistribute v1's existing curriculum ablation rather than establish new experiments.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix A.5.1 reports inter-rater agreement exceeding 0.85; v3 Appendix A.4.1 replaces this with a mean-quality claim, removing the agreement statistic. Confidence-interval plots remain. Neither version provides benchmark-wide repeated-run counts, seed information or significance testing.

E6.justification: The principal UniMedVL VQA scores and in-domain average generation FID of 96.29 remain unchanged. V3 adds extensive results, including segmentation Dice of 33.51 overall and 72% balanced accuracy in the realism study. Reconstruction values change, such as VQGAN CXR rFID from 33.57 to 18.66. Report-generation results and expert-audit figures are revised; equivalent evaluation conditions are insufficiently documented to interpret the report-score changes as performance gains.

T1.justification: V1 presents training losses without formal performance guarantees. V3 Section 3.3 and Appendix A.9 introduce a conditional mutual-information argument, a Bayes-optimal log-loss lemma, and a proposition with proofs comparing joint and factorized prediction risks. This adds a substantial theoretical component, although its guarantees concern Bayes-optimal log-loss.

C1.justification: The single-model understanding/generation contribution, large medical corpus and three-stage curriculum remain central. V3 narrows v1's superior/state-of-the-art understanding claims to competitive performance, adds a first large-scale unified medical dataset claim, and describes downstream adaptation more cautiously as effective task-specific fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's mainly positive transfer discussion and 2D restriction, v3 explains caption-fidelity tradeoffs, protocol-dependent comparisons, efficiency costs and specialist performance gaps. Appendix A.8 documents hallucinated annotations, structural distortions, counting errors and surgical-recognition failures. The conclusion explicitly limits the work to research rather than a deployable clinical solution.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a direct dataset-release link alongside the retained code link, materially expanding access information for the central corpus. It newly documents the generation train/test split, alignment-score normalization, five-expert stratified auditing and efficiency measurement controls. Core training schedules and hardware remain unchanged, while v1's Qwen2.5-7B judging-model disclosure is omitted. Resource availability itself was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Citation coverage expands to specialized generators, SAM3/Medical SAM3, ExGra-Med and newer medical evaluation work, while several broader examples are removed. The central positioning against task-specific medical systems and HealthGPT's checkpoint switching remains. Publication and bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute new research relationships.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Ablations move after the principal comparisons, appendix expert validation moves before qualitative examples, and new limitations, impact and analytical sections reorganize the argument. UniMed-5M is renamed UniMedVL-5M.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column layout with substantially reorganized displays. V1's curriculum table becomes four tables, generation metrics are split between a table and radar chart, and dataset-distribution charts are replaced by a task taxonomy. Numerous evaluation and failure displays are added, while most earlier qualitative examples are retained with revised captions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly aggregate benchmarks and successful examples, v3 provides stronger specialist comparisons, quantitative segmentation evidence and detailed failure cases, alongside more restrained clinical claims. These improve assessment of the model's capabilities and limits. The net gain is constrained by unnamed external-generation datasets, unexplained result revisions and changed fine-tuning labels on unchanged scores; the new Bayes-risk argument also does not establish superiority for the implemented training objective.
